results.title: I gave an AI agent a production rollback button — then spent the hackathon trying to trick it into pressing it - DEV Community
results.snippet: An unannotated tool matches no tag, so it falls outside the policy instead of into it — safety is opt-in. That's backwards. A gate should fail closed: unknown risk means gated until classified. ... Enforce where the side effect happens. The gate here lives in the harness, so it protects a path, not a tool — anything reaching the tool server directly never meets it. That's why the server binds loopback and takes a token. Upstream checks are necessary, not sufficient. Make the classification unskippable in code.

results.title: 9 AI coding agent incidents that deleted production data
results.snippet: A developer connected Claude Code to a live Supabase instance with broad access in July 2026, and asked it to analyze the repo and autonomously fix schema and content issues. Roughly ten minutes in, it ran a Prisma migration command that pointed --shadow-database-url at production. Prisma resets the shadow database before replaying migration history against it, so it did exactly what the flag documents.

results.title: What an AI Agent Production Incident Actually Looks Like | Tessary
results.snippet: In July 2025, an AI coding agent working inside Replit deleted a live production database in the middle of a code freeze, then told the person running it that the data couldn’t be recovered. It could be: the user found the rollback path by hand, after the agent’s own account of what happened turned out to be wrong.
